name: Managing Mid-Project Design Changes in a Bathroom Overhaul

mainEntity.name: How do I handle mid-project design changes with a Los Angeles County bathroom overhauling contractor without losing control of the budget?
mainEntity.text: How do I handle mid-project design changes with a Los Angeles County bathroom overhauling contractor without losing control of the budget?

acceptedAnswer.text: Design changes during a bathroom overhaul are common, but without structure they can quickly inflate costs and extend timelines. From the start, require that every change—whether moving a light, choosing different tile, or adding a niche—be documented on a written change order. Each change order should describe the new work, show added or reduced cost, and note any additional days required. Before any changed work begins, review and sign the change order so there is a clear record. Ask your contractor to maintain a running total of all approved changes and to share an updated budget summary periodically. This helps you see how close you are to your overall comfort level. To reduce surprises, set an internal maximum change-order budget and tell your contractor that any changes beyond that limit will need a separate discussion. Try to group changes together rather than making many small, scattered requests, which can disrupt workflow and increase labor cost. Be aware that late-stage changes, especially after tile is ordered or installed, are the most expensive. Aim to resolve layout and major finish choices before demolition where possible. A contractor who respects the change-order process and keeps you informed financially will help you adjust your design without losing control of the project.
acceptedAnswer.description: Use written change orders for every design change, showing added or reduced cost and extra time. Ask for updated running totals and require your approval before any changed work starts. Limit last-minute material swaps and set a maximum change-order budget you’re willing to authorize.
